summary: Paired foraminiferal counts and grain size are open on PANGAEA but regional: the Elbe Estuary survey (CC BY, 22 stations, living-stained and dead specimens with clay/silt/sand fractions) is the closest to the claim's variables, with Thwaites Glacier, a Mediterranean core and four older South Atlantic/other surface-sediment records also matching. ForCenS is a global planktonic census without grain size in its metadata, and OBIS has 1.5 million foraminifer presence records but no sediment texture. No dataset was found that includes gravels, current speeds or shell settling velocities.
next_step: Download the Elbe zip and the Thwaites table (each small) and confirm column names for stained vs. dead counts and gravel fraction; pre-register whether grain size is used as the current-speed proxy and whether a coarse-sediment subset exists at all.
obstacles_confirmed: Most open pairs of counts and grain size are regional shelves, estuaries or single cores.
No dataset checked reports current speed or shell settling velocity.
